newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends near day's lows, July off 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends near day's lows, July off 14 pct.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures failed to recover from early sharp dive despite a rebound in New York and the key London's July contract finished Monday with a 14 percent loss.
The aggressive sell-off, led by speculators and funds, put an end, albeit temporarily, to last week's winning streak which took prices to the highest level in 20 months.
Traders said the well-overbought market was also long overdue for a downward correction.
"It's been fund selling through the morning. It then rallied a bit on arbitrage buying and towards the close, there was liquidation again by the funds and jobbers," said one.
The market was called as much as $500 a tonne lower as arabica futures came under heavy speculative selling to end Friday some 12 percent lower.
LIFFE July came in $270 down and sank further to a low of $2,100 before finishing at $2,115, a steep $355 loss.
With the Brazilian frost scares in the background, some traders said it was still early to say that the spectacular rally in both London and New York since January was coming to an end.
"Although there was a tremendous punch in the stomach (on Friday) it was not a knock out yet," said one.

"The good news is...the uptrend line is still intact," he added. Chartwise, London's filled a key chart gap -- as seen a breakway gap -- of between $2,140 and $2,102 based on the second continuation chart.
Second-month position September was also $370 down at $2,130 after a low of $2,120.
Volume reached 10,220 lots, dominated by the three front months contracts.
New York bucked higher opening calls to head lower in early trading before recovering again. July hit a low of 247.50 cents a lb before trading 20.40 cents up at 256.00 cents at 1639 GMT.
The contract plunged by 38.40 cents, the biggest single-day loss, to end Friday at 276.40.
Brazil is at the start of the frost season. There was no frost over the weekend and no damaging cold was forceast for the coffee areas for this weekend.

Local Brazilian weathermen said the approaching new air mass was worth watching because it was coming in overland and would be arriving when the country's coffee regions were already cool from the effects of last week's air mass. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
